nodes.label: System Metrics Panel (CPU, RAM, Swap, Storage)
Clients View Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Light mode UI screenshot showing the 3X-UI Clients management interface, including sidebar navigation, overview statistics cards, and a client configuration data table.

nodes.label: Client Data Table Pattern
nodes.rationale: Data table layout for managing VPN clients. Key elements include quick actions (QR, info, edit, delete), enable toggle, online status, assigned inbound port, traffic usage tracking, and duration/expiration tracking.

nodes.label: Statistics Summary Pattern
nodes.rationale: Top-level KPI summary cards displaying counts for overall clients, online, ended, depleting, disabled, and active clients to provide a quick health overview of the system.

nodes.label: Group Management
nodes.rationale: Provides interface to add, edit, and view client groups, along with statistics such as total, empty, and populated groups.

nodes.label: Sidebar Navigation
nodes.rationale: Vertical navigation menu containing application sections: Overview, Inbounds, Clients, Groups, Nodes, Settings, Configs, and API Docs.

nodes.label: Nodes Management UI
nodes.rationale: UI screenshot showing the Nodes management interface in dark mode. Serves the purpose of monitoring node statuses and resource usage.

nodes.label: Node Metrics Summary
nodes.rationale: A layout pattern displaying aggregated node statistics (Total, Online, Offline, Avg Latency) at the top of the interface.

nodes.label: Node Details Table
nodes.rationale: A key UI element listing individual nodes with actionable controls and real-time metrics (CPU, Memory, Xray Version, Uptime).

nodes.label: Nodes Page UI
nodes.rationale: UI page managing multi-node deployment, featuring a list of nodes with their status and system metrics.

nodes.label: Dashboard Layout Pattern
nodes.rationale: Organizes information with high-level summary cards (Total Nodes, Online, Offline, Avg Latency) at the top, and a detailed data table below for individual node management.

nodes.label: Node Management Table
nodes.rationale: Displays individual nodes with toggle switches, status indicators, resource utilization (CPU, Memory), and action icons (quick actions, edit, delete).

nodes.label: Dark Mode Layout Pattern
nodes.rationale: Left sidebar navigation with categorized settings panels in a dark color scheme.

nodes.label: Bot Client Management Actions
nodes.rationale: Inline keyboard buttons allowing management of clients via Telegram bot: Refresh, Reset Traffic, Traffic Limit, Change Expiry Date, IP Log, IP Limit, Set Telegram User, and Enable/Disable.

nodes.label: Bot Client Status Display
nodes.rationale: Telegram message displaying client metrics including Email, Connection Status (Online), Expire Date, and Traffic stats (Upload/Download/Total).

nodes.label: Xray Configs Dark Mode Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Screenshot displaying the Xray configuration panel in a dark theme, showing layout patterns like sidebar navigation and tabbed content areas.

nodes.label: Tabbed Configuration Layout
nodes.rationale: Uses tabs (Basics, Routing Rules, Outbounds, etc.) to categorize complex Xray core settings, improving usability and organization.

nodes.label: Xray Core Settings Interface
nodes.rationale: Provides a comprehensive UI for adjusting core Xray parameters like Freedom Protocol Strategy, Routing Strategy, and Outbounds.

nodes.label: Dark Mode Theme
nodes.rationale: The UI utilizes a dark theme with dark backgrounds and high contrast text to reduce eye strain, an expected design pattern for modern admin dashboards.

nodes.label: Restart Required Warning
nodes.rationale: A prominent warning box indicating that changes must be saved and the Xray panel restarted, a key design decision to prevent unsaved configurations from causing confusion.

nodes.label: Dual Authentication Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Supports both session cookies (for the SPA UI) and Bearer tokens (for programmatic clients) to accommodate both browser and script-based API consumers.

nodes.label: CSRF Bypass Pattern
nodes.rationale: Bearer-token API callers bypass CSRF requirements because token auth inherently protects against CSRF, while cookie-based SPA sessions must supply an X-CSRF-Token header on unsafe requests.

nodes.label: Nested JSON Objects Pattern
nodes.rationale: Returns complex structures like settings and streamSettings as nested JSON objects instead of escaped strings to improve developer experience, though legacy string-encoded writes are still accepted for backward compatibility.

nodes.label: Slim Payload Optimization
nodes.rationale: Provides a reduced /list/slim endpoint that strips down clients to {email, enable, comment} and omits UUIDs from ClientStats to save bandwidth and improve performance on UI list pages.

nodes.label: BotFather Chat Screenshot
nodes.rationale: UI screenshot showing the process to create a Telegram bot via BotFather, including the /newbot command, name selection, and receiving the HTTP API token.

nodes.label: Telegram Bot Creation
nodes.rationale: Creation of a new Telegram bot which yields an HTTP API token for controlling the bot.
